claims.text: Phase-selective recrystallization preferentially recrystallizes the ductile fcc phase while preserving the hard B2 phase.
Phase-selective recrystallization increases strength relative to the as-cast microstructure.
Phase-selective recrystallization increases ductility relative to the as-cast microstructure.
The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
Controlled deformation followed by selective annealing can create the phase-selectively recrystallized microstructure.
Hot forging or severe plastic deformation are suitable deformation pretreatments for the proposed intervention.
An intermediate annealing temperature below the B2 coarsening threshold permits selective recrystallization.
The expected enhancement holds under quasi-static room-temperature loading.
The resulting microstructure contains a fully recrystallized soft phase embedded in an intact hard-phase skeleton.
The phase-selectively recrystallized microstructure beneficially alters strain partitioning between the two phases.
The phase-selectively recrystallized microstructure delays crack initiation at phase boundaries.
Selective recrystallization eliminates weak boundaries.
Selective recrystallization promotes homogeneous deformation in the ductile fcc phase.
The treatment releases or enhances the strain-hardening capacity of the duplex phases.
The treatment constrains dislocation motion in the hard B2 phase.
The treated alloy can attain approximately 35% uniform tensile elongation.
The treated alloy can attain yield or ultimate tensile strength around 2 GPa.
The as-cast dual-phase lamellar baseline typically has a less optimized strength-ductility balance.
Coarsening of the B2 phase or recrystallization of both phases would prevent the desired enhancement.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on temperature, strain rate, annealing time, and alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis defines the comparator as the untreated as-cast alloy, whereas the falsification experiment compares phase-selectively annealed samples only against conventionally annealed samples after deformation. Without an as-cast arm, that experiment does not directly test the stated improvement relative to the specified baseline.
